title: feat(spec): a book audience can name a capability, so Setup and Studio docs open only for callers who can open those apps
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-sales"} -->
_Requested by **Sales** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4Uu?thread=cmsg_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4UuUXusuGGFSzvb1tSB9KytgS)_

Part of #36029 — the code half. The ADR-0046 §6.7 note the ruling also names lands in its own seat-run PR (Tier H); the seat closes the card when both have merged.

Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: added
Skills-docs: none — no `skills/` page teaches the book audience forms; `content/docs/ui/doc-pages.mdx` documents the new form in this change

## 维护者速读

- 没有 Setup 权限的成员，从此在文档列表、搜索内容和直接打开文章三处都看不到 Setup 自带的帮助文档；能进 Setup 的管理员（不管通过哪个权限集拿到的）照常能看。Studio 的帮助文档同理。
- 这是「控制台 UX 改进」专题里「系统包文档只给管理员看」的收尾：以前只是列表不显示，知道地址的成员仍能打开。按你 11-24 选的方案做：文档可见范围可以写成「持有某项系统权限的人」。
- 出错时最坏是管理员也看不到这两篇帮助文档（不会多放人进来）；改动可直接撤回，不涉及存量数据。
- 无。

## What changes

Ruling of record: the maintainer's answer to the decision card, relayed in comment 7122770897 (「A 按系统权限判定」).

- **`@objectstack/spec`** — `BookAudienceSchema` / `BookAudience` gain a fourth, strict arm `{ systemPermission: string }`. `AudienceCaller` gains `systemPermissions?: readonly string[]`; `audienceAllows` admits the arm only for an authenticated caller whose list holds the token, and denies when the list is absent (fail closed, ADR-0049). The other three forms answer exactly as before. Regenerated: `content/docs/references/system/book.mdx`, the strictness-ledger count (`system/` 409 → 410, the new strict arm). Liveness row `book.audience` re-verified with the new evidence.
- **`@objectstack/rest`** — `resolveDocsAudience` treats a `{ systemPermission }` book as gated (no fast path), and `resolveAudienceCaller` fills `systemPermissions` from the caller's own context — the same list `holdsRequiredPermissions` reads for an app's `requiredPermissions`, so the Setup manual opens for exactly the callers the Setup app opens for. Holdings are read only when such a book exists; a capability-only gate never asks the security service for permission sets. New export `anySystemPermissionAudience`; new optional port `MetaReadGateAudienceSources.resolveAudienceSystemPermissions` for a transport whose audience reads someone else's holdings.
- **`@objectstack/runtime`** — the MCP docs door (`search_package_docs`, `read_package_doc`) supplies that port on a delegated OAuth envelope, so the delegating person's own capabilities decide, never the token's ceiling (the same rule its `{ permissionSet }` reading already follows, ADR-0090 D10).
- **`@objectstack/setup`, `@objectstack/studio`** — each registers a manual (`setup_manual`, `studio_manual`) claiming its own doc namespace (`include: 'setup_*'` / `'studio_*'`) with `audience: { systemPermission: 'setup.access' }` / `'studio.access'`, the token each app's `requiredPermissions` names.
- **`@objectstack/lint`** — `capability-reference-unknown` also resolves `books[].audience.systemPermission`; its `os explain` text names the new position.
- **`ui/` (`@object-ui/app-shell`, `@object-ui/i18n`)** — Studio's book preview shows a capability-gated book as "Capability: TOKEN" / 「系统权限：TOKEN」 instead of "Org", and the book form's JSON schema round-trips the new form.
- **Docs** — `content/docs/ui/doc-pages.mdx` documents the form, when to use it, and why a gated book claims by name rather than `include: '*'`; `content/docs/permissions/capabilities.mdx` names the new lint position.

Decided in the thread (small, listed here per the standing rule):
- Arm name `systemPermission` (the ruling left it to the spec lane): it is the same word as the grant side, `systemPermissions`, which is what an author writes on the permission set.
- Holdings source: the caller's own `systemPermissions` (what the app gate reads) rather than a fresh `resolvePermissionSetsForContext` pass — the ruling's intent is "every admin who can open Setup can read it", and this is that predicate exactly, with no second resolution to drift from it. The MCP door's delegated envelope reads the person's resolved grants, as before.

Why the manuals claim by namespace, not `include: '*'` (contract review S1, 7196156631): a package scope leaves out only a doc stamped with another package, so a stored doc bound to no package is in every scope. A catch-all manual would claim every such doc and take it from members. `setup_*` / `studio_*` claim exactly the package's pages; pinned in spec, REST and MCP with an unstamped control doc that stays readable by a member, and a catch-all control that shuts it.

Item 2 of the card (the other `com.objectstack.*` docs): exactly two exist on `origin/main`, `setup_overview` and `studio_overview`; both are now gated. No end-user platform help exists today, so nothing stays readable by everyone.

## Tests

All run against this branch's head; each pinned behaviour was ablated once (rebuild, change, watch it red, restore).

<details><summary>Targeted suites</summary>

- `packages/spec` `src/system/book.test.ts` — 50/50 (parse of the arm, strictness, `audienceAllows`, set ≠ capability both ways, fail closed, `resolveDocAudiences` union with a `{ systemPermission }` book).
- `packages/lint` `src/validate-capability-references.test.ts` — 22/22 (typo at `books[2].audience.systemPermission` warns; built-in and granted tokens pass; other forms resolve nothing).
- `packages/rest` `src/meta-doc-system-permission-audience.test.ts` (new) — 14/14 (2 added for S1: an unstamped doc beside both manuals is listed, carried with content and read by a member; a catch-all control 403s it): a member without the capability gets the Setup doc in neither `GET /meta/doc` nor `?include=content` (body absent from the whole answer), `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` on `GET /meta/doc/:name`, the book absent from `GET /meta/book` and `403` on its tree, nothing from the implicit package book either; a holder reads all of it; a non-list `systemPermissions` denies; anonymous 401; no permission-set resolution for a capability-only gate; fast-path control.
- `packages/runtime` `src/domains/mcp-package-docs.test.ts` — 28/28 (7 new; S1: unstamped doc found and read beside a namespaced manual, catch-all control closed; session holder / non-holder, set-named-like-capability stays closed, no list fails closed, OAuth person decides, OAuth envelope capability opens nothing — no union).
- `packages/qa/dogfood` `test/setup-docs-audience.dogfood.test.ts` (new) — 3/3 on a real boot with the real `createSetupAppPlugin()`: precondition (member 403 on the Setup app, admin 200), member refused on all three doors, admin reads all three plus the manual's tree.
- `ui` `packages/app-shell/.../adminPreviews.i18n-10862-s2.test.tsx` — 42/42 (new case per language for the capability chip).

</details>

<details><summary>Ablations</summary>

- REST: `needSystemPermissions: false` → the 3 holder pins red (12 → 9 pass).
- MCP: delegated override removed → the 2 OAuth pins red (26 → 24).
- Setup: `books: []` → both dogfood door pins red (the member reads the doc again — the pre-fix behaviour reproduced on a real boot).

</details>

## Acceptance notes

- The Setup/Studio docs' Console address changes from the implicit book (`/apps/com.objectstack.setup/docs/com.objectstack.setup/setup_overview`) to the manual (`.../docs/setup/setup_overview`). No link in the repo names the old one; the flat `/docs/setup_overview` permalink still finds the page.
- The manual card on the "All docs" page is now labelled by the book (`Setup` / `Studio`, English) where the implicit book borrowed the app's translated label. Platform packages ship no `books.*.label` bundle today; noted, not filed.
- Docs-door fast path: in a deployment that installs Setup or Studio, some book is now gated, so `allReadable` is false and every doc read, doc list and app-nav doc gate reads the doc corpus and runs the audience pass. Correct, and the price of the ruling; a follow-up if the docs doors show up in a profile.
- A `{ permissionSet, systemPermission }` object (both keys) parses as the `{ permissionSet }` arm with the other key dropped, because that older arm is not strict; making it strict is a narrowing and out of scope.
- Comment drift (carried from the earlier os-dev report on this card): the NOTE (transitional) header in `packages/apps/setup/src/index.ts` says the package is not yet wired into dev/serve; it is (`packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-dev/src/dev-plugin.ts`). Left as is.

## Verification

Read first: `packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts` (`resolveAudienceCaller`, `resolveDocsAudience`) — the one place the new holdings are read; then `packages/spec/src/system/book.zod.ts` (`audienceAllows`); then `packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp-package-docs.ts` (`packageDocsReadGate`).

Two-minute check: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/dogfood exec vitest run test/setup-docs-audience.dogfood.test.ts` — expect 3 passed: a plain member is refused the Setup doc on every door, the admin reads it.

L2 owed at CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER (Clause-② widening on `packages/spec/src`), by the seat — not self-reviewed here.
